title: Nilpotent coefficient extensions preserve a common higher direct-image bound
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq R$ an ideal, and $t\geq1$ an integer such that $I^t=0$. Use the categories $\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\mathrm{et}},R)$ of sheaves of modules over the constant coefficient sheaf on the small etale site, and similarly for $R/I$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Write $R^qf_*^R$ and $R^qf_*^{R/I}$ for the higher direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For every integer $N$, if $R^qf_*^{R/I}Q=0$ for every sheaf $Q$ of $R/I$-modules and every integer $q\geq0$ with $q>N$, then $R^qf_*^RM=0$ for every sheaf $M$ of $R$-modules and every integer $q\geq0$ with $q>N$. The same integer $N$ works independently of $t$; no finiteness or flatness of $M$ is required.

source.place: Tag 015B, label lemma-higher-derived-functors, part (1): the long exact sequence. The nilpotent-coefficient application is agent-written, extracting the coefficient-filtration argument in Bhatt-Scholze Lemma 6.5.11 and the former step 5 of the item; coefficient-change vanishing is the existing lem-sbc-coefficient-higher-direct-image-zero.

proof.text: For the underlying presheaf P of M define P_j(U) = I^j M(U), with restrictions induced from P. The map_smul identity makes these submodules a presheaf. Ideal multiplication gives I P_j(U) = I^(j+1) M(U), using Submodule.mem_smul_top_iff and Submodule.mul_smul. Hence the inclusion P_(j+1) to P_j followed by the quotient P_j to P_j / I P_j is a sectionwise short exact sequence. The quotient presheaf with coefficients R/I and its restriction to R are constructed by the already proved ModuleCat.quotSMulTop functor and its restriction-of-scalars equivalence. This is the elementary descending I-adic filtration, replacing the annihilator filtration.

The category of sheaves with values in ModuleCat R is Grothendieck abelian and presheafToSheaf is exact, by clause (1) of lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed. Therefore sheafifying the sequences of step 1 gives short exact sequences. Restriction of scalars along R to R/I commutes with sheafification: it is left adjoint to coextension of scalars, and the sheafification universal property supplies the canonical comparison isomorphism (sheafComposeNatIso). Thus the third term is the R-restriction of a sheaf Q_j of R/I-modules.

Fix an integer q >= 0 with q > N, and write q as the cast of a natural number. The assumed bound vanishes on every Q_j. Apply lem-sbc-coefficient-higher-direct-image-zero to Ideal.Quotient.mk I and the qcqs morphism f to get vanishing after restriction to R, then transport it across the isomorphism in step 2.

Use the existing ModuleCat-valued lowerStar instances for additivity and preservation of finite limits, as recorded on lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-left-exact. The sheaf category of step 2 has enough injectives by lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives. The single-object comparison lem-sp-derived-functor-single-identification identifies higherDirectImage with the q-th classical right derived functor of lowerStar. Applying lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact to each short exact sequence gives an exact segment at its middle object, including q=0. When the two outer objects are zero, so is the middle object (ShortComplex.Exact.isZero_of_both_isZero).

The presheaf P_t is zero because I^t = 0; sheafification and the additive q-th right derived functor preserve zero objects. Descending induction from t to 0 now uses steps 3 and 4 to show that every sheafified P_j has zero q-th direct image. P_0 is canonically isomorphic to P since I^0 is the unit ideal; the sheafification of P is M. Transporting across these isomorphisms proves the assertion. Every step keeps q fixed, so N is unchanged, including the case N < 0 and q = 0.
